issuer: the Road Safety Authority, the licensing authority
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Irish Statute Book (the Office of the Attorney General). The Road Traffic (Licensing of Drivers) Regulations 2006 (S.I. 537/2006) as amended by the Road Traffic (Licensing of Drivers) (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2011 (S.I. 483/2011, in operation from 19 January 2013), which replaced Regulation 9 and Regulation 10(2): 17 is the age below which a person is disqualified from holding a driving licence or a learner permit for category B, so the full licence is held from 17 (the learner permit's time before the test isn't read here); a licence for category B granted to someone under 60 is for 10 years plus the unexpired period of a licence held before (the unexpired part not held). The Amendment Regulations 2013 (S.I. 6/2013) made the Road Safety Authority the licensing authority, retaining the fees. The Road Traffic (Licensing of Drivers) (Fees) Regulations 2024 (S.I. 673/2024, in operation from 1 January 2025, revoking those of 2020) set the fee for a 10-year (or longer than 3-year) driving licence at €65 (a learner permit €45, not held). The Irish Statute Book publishes statutory instruments as made, not consolidated: no instrument after S.I. 673/2024 changing these fees was found, and the age and term are as S.I. 483/2011 set them, with no later change to Regulations 9 and 10 found. The National Driver Licence Service's own site answered a Cloudflare check and was not read. No identity card is held (the RSA's public services card isn't its), and no exchange list was read.

sources.said: These Regulations come into operation on 19 January 2013. ... the age set out in column (2) of the Table below opposite the mention of a vehicle category in column (1) of the Table is the age below which a person is disqualified from holding a driving licence or a learner permit in respect of vehicles of that category. ... B, BE 17 ... in the case of an applicant less than 60 years of age on the commencement day, for a licence to drive vehicles of category A, A1, A2, AM, B, BE or W, 10 years plus the unexpired period of a licence previously granted to the applicant
